source.text: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰποῦσα ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἐφώνησεν Μαριὰμ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς λάθρᾳ εἰποῦσα· Ὁ διδάσκαλος πάρεστιν καὶ φωνεῖ σε.

records.literal_gloss: And this having said she went away and called Mary the sister of her secretly, having said, "The Teacher is present and calls you."

en.L: And having said this, she went away and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, "The Teacher is here and is calling you."
en.B: When she had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside privately. "The Teacher is here," she said, "and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is calling for you."
en.R: After saying this, Martha went back to the house. She took her sister Mary aside and told her quietly, "The Teacher is here, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is asking for you."

es.L: Y habiendo dicho esto, se fue y llamó a María su hermana en secreto, diciendo: «El Maestro está aquí y te llama».
es.B: Dicho esto, volvió y llamó aparte a su hermana María. «El Maestro está aquí», le dijo, «y te llama».
es.R: Después de decir esto, Marta volvió a la casa. Llamó aparte a su hermana María y le dijo en voz baja: «El Maestro está aquí, y pregunta por ti».

fr.L: Et ayant dit cela, elle s’en alla et appela en secret Marie, sa sœur, en disant : « Le Maître est là, et [{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}] t’appelle. »
fr.B: Après avoir dit cela, elle s’en retourna appeler sa sœur Marie et lui dit à part : « Le Maître est là, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te demande. »
fr.R: Après avoir dit cela, Marthe est retournée à la maison. Elle a pris sa sœur Marie à part et lui a dit tout bas : « Le Maître est là, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te demande. »

sw.L: Na alipokwisha kusema haya, akaenda akamwita Mariamu dada yake kwa siri, akisema, "Mwalimu yupo, anakuita."
sw.B: Alipokwisha kusema hayo, alirudi akamwita dada yake Mariamu faraghani. "Mwalimu yupo hapa," akasema, "{{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anakuita."
sw.R: Baada ya kusema hayo, Martha alirudi nyumbani. Akamchukua dada yake Mariamu kando, akamwambia kwa sauti ya chini, "Mwalimu yupo hapa, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anakuulizia."

vi.L: Nói điều này xong, cô đi về và kín đáo gọi Ma-ri, em gái mình, nói rằng: "Thầy đang ở đây và gọi em."
vi.B: Nói xong, cô trở về gọi riêng Ma-ri, em gái mình: "Thầy đến rồi, và Thầy đang gọi em."
vi.R: Nói xong, Ma-thê trở về nhà. Cô kéo riêng Ma-ri, em gái mình, ra và nói nhỏ: "Thầy đến rồi. Thầy đang hỏi em đó."

ko.L: 그는 이 말을 하고 가서 자기 자매 마리아를 남몰래 불러 말했다. "선생님께서 여기 계시는데 너를 부르신다."
ko.B: 이렇게 말하고 나서 마르다는 돌아가 자기 자매 마리아를 조용히 따로 불러 말했다. "선생님께서 오셔서 너를 부르신다."
ko.R: 이렇게 말한 뒤에 마르다는 집으로 돌아갔다. 그리고 자매 마리아를 한쪽으로 데려가 조용히 말했다. "선생님께서 오셨는데, 너를 찾으신다."

decisions.choice: secretly: privately, out of the hearing of the mourners in the house
alternatives: so that word of Jesus's coming would not reach those who might report him to the authorities
so that Mary could meet Jesus alone
decisions.reason: Mary was in the house with the people who had come to console her (11:19-20, 31). Martha speaks to her quietly, aside from them. John does not say why. The danger to Jesus near Jerusalem has just been mentioned (11:8, 16), and some of these same visitors later go to the Pharisees (11:46), but Martha may simply have wanted her sister to meet Jesus before the crowd did. In the event the mourners follow her anyway (11:31).

decisions.choice: the Teacher: the title Jesus's followers used for him
decisions.reason: John translates the title Rabbi as Teacher (1:38; 20:16), and Jesus says that his disciples call him "Teacher" and "Lord" (13:13). With the article it is the name the household used for him: Mary knows at once whom Martha means.

decisions.choice: is calling you: Jesus has asked for Mary; possibly an echo of the shepherd who calls his own
decisions.reason: John has not told us that Jesus asked for Mary; we learn it from Martha's words. The verb is the one used of the shepherd who "calls his own sheep by name" and is followed by them (10:3), and Mary rises at once (11:29). The link is possible but not certain.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for God or Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting: he, him and his for Jesus, "you" and "me" in his prayer (verses 41-42), and "you" when Mary speaks to him. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: Martha went back to the house
decisions.reason: Readable names Martha and says where she went: Mary had stayed sitting in the house (11:20).

decisions.choice: Marta volvió a la casa
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names Martha and says where she went (11:20). Spanish needs no pronoun for Jesus here ("te llama").

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("ils lui disent", "il vient", "Jésus dit", 11:34-44); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (11:28-44), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("s’en alla", "tomba", "cria") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (verses 34, 38, 39, 40, 44), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("Marthe est retournée"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. The imperfect is used for what was going on ("venait", "était encore", "disaient").

decisions.choice: le Maître (every level); il te demande (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Maître" is the word French uses for "Rabbi" in 1:38 and for a respected teacher; "enseignant" and "professeur" name a job and are not used as a title (meaning decision m2). "Il te demande" is the everyday way to say that someone is asking for you; Literal keeps "t’appelle", the verb of the shepherd calling his own (m3), and brackets the subject French needs.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "the Teacher", repeated in place of "he" (B, R) with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: "Thầy" is both the title the followers used and the word for teacher; as a noun of address it is always capitalised and takes no span (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: "em" for Mary in her elder sister's words
decisions.reason: An elder sister calls her younger sister "em"; this follows the choice of Martha as the elder (11:1).

decisions.choice: "선생님께서 ... 부르신다": Martha speaks to her sister in the plain style (해라체) with the honorific -시- for Jesus
decisions.reason: Between sisters the plain style is natural (style guide, section 4); "선생님" with the honorific is how a follower speaks of her Teacher.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; "선생님께서", "께" and the honorific -시- carry respect
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7); recorded once for this passage.

source.text: ἐκείνη δὲ ὡς ἤκουσεν ἠγέρθη ταχὺ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: That [one] and when she heard rose quickly and was coming to him;

en.L: And when she heard [it], she rose quickly and was coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: As soon as Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: When Mary heard this, she jumped up and hurried out to Jesus.

es.L: Y ella, al oír[lo], se levantó deprisa y venía hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: En cuanto María lo oyó, se levantó deprisa y fue hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Cuando María oyó esto, se levantó de un salto y salió corriendo a ver a Jesús.

fr.L: Et elle, quand elle [l’]entendit, se leva vite et venait vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Dès que Marie entendit cela, elle se leva en hâte et alla vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Quand Marie a entendu cela, elle s’est levée d’un bond et elle a couru vers Jésus.

sw.L: Naye aliposikia, aliinuka upesi, akawa anakuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Mariamu aliposikia hayo, aliinuka upesi akaenda {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: Mariamu aliposikia hayo, aliruka akaondoka haraka kwenda kwa Yesu.

vi.L: Còn cô ấy, khi nghe [vậy], liền vội đứng dậy và đi đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Vừa nghe vậy, Ma-ri vội đứng dậy đi đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Nghe vậy, Ma-ri liền đứng bật dậy và vội vã đi ra gặp Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 마리아는 듣고 재빨리 일어나 그분께로 가고 있었다.
ko.B: 마리아는 그 말을 듣자마자 급히 일어나 그분께 갔다.
ko.R: 마리아는 이 말을 듣고 벌떡 일어나 서둘러 예수께 갔다.

decisions.choice: rose quickly: she had been sitting at home in mourning and got up at once
decisions.reason: Mary had stayed sitting in the house (11:20). Mourners sat with the bereaved (compare Job 2:13), and the family received visitors there. She gets up as soon as she hears that Jesus is asking for her. The quickness is repeated in verse 31, where the visitors notice it.

decisions.choice: was coming: she set out toward him, and the story pauses before she arrives
decisions.reason: The tense pictures her on her way. Verse 30 then stops to say where Jesus was, and verse 32 tells of her reaching him.

decisions.choice: went to him (B); hurried out to Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say simply that she went; Readable's "hurried" carries over the haste of "quickly" (meaning decision m1) and "out" anticipates verse 30, where Jesus is still outside the village.

decisions.choice: fue hacia él (B); salió corriendo (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable carries over the haste of "deprisa".

source.text: οὔπω δὲ ἐληλύθει ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν κώμην, ἀλλ’ ἦν ἔτι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα.

records.literal_gloss: Not yet now had come the Jesus into the village, but was still in the place where met him the Martha.

en.L: Now Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Jesus had not yet come into the village; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still at the place where Martha had met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus had not come into the village yet. He was still at the place where Martha had met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Jesús todavía no había entrado en la aldea, sino que estaba aún en el lugar donde Marta {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había encontrado.
es.B: Jesús todavía no había entrado en la aldea; seguía en el lugar donde Marta {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había encontrado.
es.R: Jesús todavía no había entrado en la aldea. Seguía en el lugar donde Marta se había encontrado con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Or Jésus n’était pas encore venu dans le village, mais [{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}] était encore à l’endroit où Marthe {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait rencontré.
fr.B: Jésus n’était pas encore entré dans le village ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se trouvait toujours à l’endroit où Marthe {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait rencontré.
fr.R: Jésus n’était pas encore entré dans le village. Il était encore à l’endroit où Marthe {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait rencontré.

sw.L: Basi Yesu alikuwa bado hajaingia kijijini, bali alikuwa bado mahali pale Martha alipokutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Yesu alikuwa bado hajaingia kijijini; alikuwa bado pale mahali Martha alipokutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa bado hajaingia kijijini. Alikuwa bado pale mahali Martha alipokutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

vi.L: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu chưa vào làng, nhưng vẫn còn ở nơi Ma-thê đã gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu chưa vào làng; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn còn ở chỗ Ma-thê đã gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu chưa vào trong làng. Ngài vẫn còn ở chỗ Ma-thê đã gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그런데 예수께서는 아직 마을에 들어오지 않으시고, 마르다가 그분을 맞이했던 곳에 여전히 계셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 아직 마을에 들어오지 않으셨고, 마르다가 그분을 맞이했던 곳에 그대로 계셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 아직 마을에 들어오지 않으셨다. 마르다를 만나셨던 그곳에 아직 계셨다.

decisions.choice: a note of background: Jesus had stayed outside the village
decisions.reason: John pauses to explain where Jesus was. It explains why Mary had to go out (verse 29) and why the mourners, seeing her leave, thought she was going to the tomb (verse 31): tombs lay outside the village.

decisions.choice: the place where Martha had met him: outside Bethany, on the way in
decisions.reason: Martha had gone out to meet him when she heard he was coming (11:20). John does not say why Jesus waited there; it may have been to meet the sisters away from the crowd in the house, but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: had met
decisions.reason: The meeting took place earlier (11:20), so every level puts it further in the past than the main story.

source.text: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι οἱ ὄντες μετ’ αὐτῆς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ παραμυθούμενοι αὐτήν, ἰδόντες τὴν Μαριὰμ ὅτι ταχέως ἀνέστη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν, ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῇ δόξαντες ὅτι ὑπάγει εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἵνα κλαύσῃ ἐκεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore Jews the [ones] being with her in the house and consoling her, having seen the Mary that quickly she rose up and went out, followed her, having supposed that she is going to the tomb that she might weep there.

en.L: So the Jews who were with her in the house and consoling her, having seen that Mary rose up quickly and went out, followed her, supposing that she was going to the tomb to weep there.
en.B: The Jews who were with Mary in the house, comforting her, saw her get up quickly and go out. They followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep there.
en.R: The Jews who had come to comfort Mary were with her in the house. When they saw her get up quickly and go out, they went after her. They thought she was going to the tomb to cry there.

es.L: Los judíos, pues, que estaban con ella en casa y la consolaban, al ver que María se levantó deprisa y salió, la siguieron, pensando que iba al sepulcro a llorar allí.
es.B: Los judíos que estaban con María en la casa consolándola la vieron levantarse deprisa y salir. La siguieron, pensando que iba al sepulcro a llorar allí.
es.R: Los judíos que habían venido a consolar a María estaban con ella en la casa. Cuando la vieron levantarse deprisa y salir, fueron tras ella. Pensaban que iba a la tumba a llorar allí.

fr.L: Les Juifs donc qui étaient avec elle dans la maison et qui la consolaient, ayant vu que Marie s’était levée vite et était sortie, la suivirent, pensant qu’elle allait au tombeau afin d’y pleurer.
fr.B: Les Juifs qui étaient avec Marie dans la maison pour la consoler la virent se lever en hâte et sortir. Ils la suivirent, pensant qu’elle allait au tombeau pour y pleurer.
fr.R: Les Juifs qui étaient venus consoler Marie étaient avec elle dans la maison. Quand ils l’ont vue se lever vite et sortir, ils l’ont suivie. Ils pensaient qu’elle allait à la tombe pour y pleurer.

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi waliokuwa pamoja naye nyumbani wakimfariji, walipomwona Mariamu ameinuka upesi na kutoka, wakamfuata, wakidhani kwamba anakwenda kaburini kulia huko.
sw.B: Wayahudi waliokuwa pamoja na Mariamu nyumbani wakimfariji walimwona akiinuka upesi na kutoka. Wakamfuata, wakidhani kwamba anakwenda kaburini kulia huko.
sw.R: Wayahudi waliokuja kumfariji Mariamu walikuwa pamoja naye nyumbani. Walipomwona akiinuka upesi na kutoka, walimfuata. Walidhani anakwenda kaburini kulia huko.

vi.L: Vậy những người Do Thái đang ở với cô trong nhà và an ủi cô, khi thấy Ma-ri vội vàng đứng dậy và đi ra, thì đi theo cô, tưởng rằng cô đi ra mộ để khóc ở đó.
vi.B: Những người Do Thái đang ở trong nhà với Ma-ri để an ủi cô thấy cô vội đứng dậy đi ra ngoài. Họ đi theo cô, nghĩ rằng cô ra mộ để khóc ở đó.
vi.R: Những người Do Thái đến an ủi Ma-ri đang ở với cô trong nhà. Khi thấy cô vội đứng dậy đi ra ngoài, họ đi theo cô. Họ tưởng cô ra mộ để khóc ở đó.

ko.L: 그래서 집에서 마리아와 함께 있으면서 그를 위로하던 유대인들은, 마리아가 급히 일어나 나가는 것을 보고, 그가 무덤에 울러 간다고 생각하여 그를 따라갔다.
ko.B: 집에서 마리아와 함께 있으면서 그를 위로하던 유대인들은 마리아가 급히 일어나 나가는 것을 보았다. 그들은 마리아가 무덤에 가서 울려는 줄 알고 그 뒤를 따라갔다.
ko.R: 마리아를 위로하러 온 유대인들이 집 안에 마리아와 함께 있었다. 그들은 마리아가 급히 일어나 나가는 것을 보고 뒤따라갔다. 마리아가 무덤에 가서 울려는 줄로 생각했던 것이다.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the friends and neighbors who had come from Jerusalem to console the sisters
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: These are the many who had come to Martha and Mary to console them about their brother (11:19), and they are named here by what they were doing: staying with Mary in the house and comforting her. They are mourners, not the authorities. Some of them later believe in Jesus and some report to the Pharisees (11:45-46). Martha, Mary and Lazarus are Jews as well, as is Jesus himself (4:9).

decisions.choice: thinking (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The older manuscripts, among them the earliest papyri of John, say that the visitors followed Mary "thinking" that she was going to the tomb. Many later manuscripts read "saying", which makes the reason a remark they made to one another. The sense of the story is the same. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: to weep at the tomb: mourners went to the grave to lament
decisions.reason: Friends came to sit with a bereaved family and grieve with them in the days after a burial (11:19), and mourners went out to the tomb to lament there. The verb for weeping is the ordinary word for crying aloud in grief, the same word used of Mary and the mourners in verse 33. It is not the word used of Jesus in verse 35.

decisions.choice: she was going: what they supposed, told in their own present tense
decisions.reason: Greek keeps the tense of the thought itself ("she is going"); the sense is what they thought at that moment. They were mistaken: she was going to Jesus.

decisions.choice: The Jews who were with Mary (B); The Jews who had come to comfort Mary (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners present in the house (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people in the scene, as 10:31 does, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew or the authorities. Readable draws "had come to comfort" from verse 19.

decisions.choice: cry
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for the loud weeping of the mourners here and in verse 33, and keeps a different wording for Jesus's tears in verse 35, as the Greek does (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: los judíos (every level)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners from Jerusalem in this scene (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les Juifs qui étaient avec Marie (B); les Juifs qui étaient venus consoler Marie (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners who had come to comfort the sisters (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so no level speaks of leaders. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people in the house, as the English does; the same holds in verses 33 and 36.

decisions.choice: "người Do Thái" at every level in 11:31-36
decisions.reason: The meaning decisions name friends and mourners, not the authorities, so B and R keep the people's name.

decisions.choice: "유대인들" at every level, not "유대 지도자들"
decisions.reason: Here they are friends and neighbors who came to mourn (meaning decision), so Balanced and Readable keep "유대인들"; this holds for 11:33, 11:36 and 11:37.

source.text: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ ὡς ἦλθεν ὅπου ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἔπεσεν αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς πόδας, λέγουσα αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἄν μου ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore Mary when she came where was Jesus, having seen him, fell of him at the feet, saying to him, "Lord, if you were here, not would of me have died the brother."

en.L: So Mary, when she came where Jesus was [and] saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, fell at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had been here, my brother would not have died."
en.B: When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, she fell at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, had {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} been here, my brother would not have died."
en.R: Mary came to the place where Jesus was. When she saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, she fell down at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. "Lord," she said, "if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had been here, my brother would still be alive."

es.L: María, pues, cuando llegó adonde estaba Jesús, al verlo, cayó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, diciéndole: «Señor, si hubieras estado aquí, mi hermano no habría muerto».
es.B: Cuando María llegó adonde estaba Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vio, cayó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Señor, si hubieras estado aquí, mi hermano no habría muerto».
es.R: María llegó al lugar donde estaba Jesús. Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vio, se echó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies. «Señor», {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo, «si hubieras estado aquí, mi hermano todavía estaría vivo».

fr.L: Marie donc, quand elle arriva là où était Jésus, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voyant, tomba à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disant : « Seigneur, si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avais été ici, mon frère ne serait pas mort. »
fr.B: Quand Marie arriva à l’endroit où était Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} vit, elle tomba à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Seigneur, si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avais été ici, mon frère ne serait pas mort. »
fr.R: Marie est arrivée à l’endroit où était Jésus. Quand elle {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a vu, elle s’est jetée à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds. « Seigneur, a-t-elle dit, si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avais été ici, mon frère serait encore vivant. »

sw.L: Basi Mariamu, alipofika mahali Yesu alipokuwa [na] kumwona, alianguka miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}, akimwambia, "Bwana, kama ungalikuwa hapa, kaka yangu asingalikufa."
sw.B: Mariamu alipofika mahali Yesu alipokuwa na kumwona, alianguka miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}, akamwambia, "Bwana, kama ungekuwa hapa, kaka yangu asingekufa."
sw.R: Mariamu alifika mahali Yesu alipokuwa. Alipomwona, alianguka chini miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}. "Bwana," akasema, "kama ungekuwa hapa, kaka yangu angekuwa bado hai."

vi.L: Vậy khi Ma-ri đến nơi Đức Giê-xu đang ở [và] thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì ngã xuống dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thưa: "Thưa Chúa, nếu Chúa đã ở đây thì anh con đã không chết."
vi.B: Khi Ma-ri đến chỗ Đức Giê-xu và thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cô sấp mình dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và thưa: "Thưa Chúa, giá mà Chúa có ở đây thì anh con đã không chết."
vi.R: Ma-ri đến chỗ Đức Giê-xu. Khi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cô quỳ sụp xuống dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và thưa: "Thưa Chúa, nếu Chúa có mặt ở đây thì anh con vẫn còn sống."

ko.L: 그래서 마리아는 예수께서 계신 곳에 와서 그분을 보고 그분의 발 앞에 엎드려 그분께 말했다. "주님, 주님께서 여기 계셨더라면 제 형제가 죽지 않았을 것입니다."
ko.B: 마리아는 예수께서 계신 곳에 이르러 그분을 보자, 그 발 앞에 엎드려 말했다. "주님, 주님께서 여기에 계셨더라면 제 형제는 죽지 않았을 것입니다."
ko.R: 마리아는 예수께서 계신 곳으로 갔다. 그리고 예수를 보자 그 발 앞에 엎드려 말했다. "주님, 주님께서 여기 계셨더라면 제 형제는 지금도 살아 있을 것입니다."

decisions.choice: fell at his feet: she threw herself down before him in grief and appeal
decisions.reason: To fall at someone's feet showed deep respect and was the posture of one who pleads or grieves. Mary is the one found at Jesus's feet elsewhere too: she anoints his feet in 12:3, as John has already said (11:2).

decisions.choice: Lord: the address of a disciple
decisions.reason: Mary and her family are among those Jesus loves (11:5), and Mary is the one who anointed him (11:2). She speaks as his follower, as Martha did (11:21, 27).

decisions.choice: if you had been here, my brother would not have died: a condition contrary to fact, the same words as Martha's
decisions.reason: Mary says almost exactly what Martha said (11:21): both sisters had believed that Jesus could heal their brother if he came in time. Grief and trust are both in the words. Unlike Martha, Mary says nothing more (compare 11:22). Her word for "my" comes earlier than in Martha's sentence, which may lay a little more weight on her own loss.

decisions.choice: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (L); Lord, had you been here, my brother would not have died (B); ... my brother would still be alive (R)
decisions.reason: Every level gives Mary the same English words as Martha in 11:21, so that the repetition stays visible (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: the same words as Martha's (11:21)
decisions.reason: As in English: every level gives Mary the same Spanish words as Martha (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Mary: "Thưa Chúa", "Chúa" for "you", "con" for herself, in the same words as Martha (11:21)
decisions.reason: The two sisters say the same thing; the Vietnamese keeps their words identical so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: Mary's words are worded exactly as Martha's in 11:21 at each level, in 합쇼체 with "주님"
decisions.reason: The Greek gives the two sisters the same sentence; Korean keeps them identical so readers notice.

source.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ὡς εἶδεν αὐτὴν κλαίουσαν καὶ τοὺς συνελθόντας αὐτῇ Ἰουδαίους κλαίοντας ἐνεβριμήσατο τῷ πνεύματι καὶ ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτόν, καὶ εἶπεν· Ποῦ τεθείκατε αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Jesus therefore when he saw her weeping and the [ones] having come with her Jews weeping, was indignant in the spirit and troubled himself, \v 34 and said, "Where have you laid him?"

en.L: So Jesus, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw her weeping and the Jews who had come with her weeping, was indignant in spirit and troubled {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, \v 34 and said, "Where have you laid him?"
en.B: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping too, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was deeply indignant in spirit and greatly troubled. \v 34 "Where have you laid him?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked.
en.R: Jesus saw Mary crying, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the Jews who had come with her crying too. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} felt angry deep in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was very troubled. \v 34 "Where did you bury him?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked.

es.L: Jesús, pues, cuando la vio llorando, y a los judíos que habían venido con ella llorando, se indignó en espíritu y se turbó, \v 34 y dijo: «¿Dónde lo {{plural_you:han puesto|habéis puesto}}?».
es.B: Cuando Jesús la vio llorar, y vio llorar también a los judíos que habían venido con ella, se indignó profundamente en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} espíritu y se conmovió mucho. \v 34 «¿Dónde lo {{plural_you:han puesto|habéis puesto}}?», preguntó.
es.R: Jesús vio a María llorando, y vio que los judíos que habían venido con ella también lloraban. Entonces sintió un enojo profundo en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} espíritu y se turbó mucho. \v 34 «¿Dónde lo {{plural_you:enterraron|enterrasteis}}?», preguntó.

fr.L: Jésus donc, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la vit pleurer, et pleurer aussi les Juifs qui étaient venus avec elle, s’indigna dans [{{deity_pronoun:son|Son}}] esprit et se troubla {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, \v 34 et dit : « Où l’avez-vous déposé ? »
fr.B: Quand Jésus la vit pleurer, et les Juifs venus avec elle pleurer aussi, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut profondément indigné en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} esprit et bouleversé. \v 34 « Où l’avez-vous mis ? » demanda-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}.
fr.R: Jésus a vu Marie pleurer, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vu pleurer aussi les Juifs qui étaient venus avec elle. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est senti en colère au plus profond de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été très troublé. \v 34 « Où l’avez-vous enterré ? » a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} demandé.

sw.L: Basi Yesu, alipomwona akilia, na Wayahudi waliokuja pamoja naye wakilia, alighadhibika rohoni, akajifadhaisha {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, \v 34 akasema, "Mmemweka wapi?"
sw.B: Yesu alipomwona akilia, na Wayahudi waliokuja pamoja naye wakilia pia, alighadhibika sana rohoni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, akafadhaika sana. \v 34 "Mmemweka wapi?" akauliza.
sw.R: Yesu alimwona Mariamu akilia, na akawaona Wayahudi waliokuja pamoja naye wakilia pia. Ndipo akasikia hasira ndani kabisa rohoni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, akafadhaika sana. \v 34 "Mlimzika wapi?" akauliza.

vi.L: Vậy khi Đức Giê-xu thấy cô khóc, và những người Do Thái cùng đến với cô cũng khóc, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phẫn nộ trong tâm linh và tự để mình xao động, \v 34 và nói: "Các người đã đặt anh ấy ở đâu?"
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu thấy cô khóc, và những người Do Thái cùng đến với cô cũng khóc, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vô cùng phẫn nộ trong tâm linh và rất xao động. \v 34 Ngài hỏi: "Các người đặt anh ấy ở đâu?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu thấy Ma-ri khóc, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy những người Do Thái đi cùng cô cũng khóc. Bấy giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cảm thấy giận dữ sâu trong lòng, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rất xao động. \v 34 Ngài hỏi: "Các người chôn anh ấy ở đâu?"

ko.L: 그래서 예수께서는 그가 우는 것과 그와 함께 온 유대인들도 우는 것을 보시고, 영으로 분개하시고 스스로 괴로워하셨다. \v 34 그리고 말씀하셨다. "너희는 그를 어디에 두었느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서는 마리아가 우는 것과 그와 함께 온 유대인들도 우는 것을 보시고, 속 깊이 분개하시며 몹시 괴로워하셨다. \v 34 그리고 "그를 어디에 뉘었느냐?" 하고 물으셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 마리아가 우는 것을 보셨다. 마리아와 함께 온 유대인들도 우는 것을 보셨다. 그러자 예수께서는 마음속 깊이 화가 나셨고, 몹시 괴로워하셨다. \v 34 예수께서 "나사로를 어디에 묻었느냐?" 하고 물으셨다.

decisions.choice: was indignant: a strong stirring of anger
alternatives: was deeply moved, with grief or compassion
decisions.reason: Wherever else this verb is used it speaks of anger or sternness: Jesus "sternly warned" men he had healed (Matthew 9:30; Mark 1:43), and some at Bethany "scolded" the woman who anointed him (Mark 14:5). In wider Greek it could describe the snorting of a horse. So the word points to indignation rather than to sorrow alone, and it comes again in verse 38. Because tears follow (verse 35), it is often taken more softly as deep emotion. A footnote gives "deeply moved".

decisions.choice: John does not say what roused his anger; the setting points to death and its grip on those he loves
alternatives: anger at the unbelief shown in the weeping
anger at the mourners' show of grief
anger at the power of evil behind death
decisions.reason: Jesus is roused as he sees Mary and the mourners weeping at the grave of his friend. Some read it as anger at their lack of trust, since Mary has just said that he came too late (verse 32) and some will soon criticize him (verse 37). Others see indignation at death itself and the misery it brings, which he is about to overturn (11:25). John states the feeling without naming its object.

decisions.choice: in spirit, and troubled himself: within his own human spirit he was shaken
decisions.reason: "Spirit" here is Jesus's own inner self, as in 13:21 ("troubled in spirit"); verse 38 says the same thing with "within himself". The verb "troubled" is the one used of Jesus facing his death (12:27; 13:21) and of the disciples' hearts (14:1). With "himself" as its object it describes a deep inner agitation which he does not hold back.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the mourners who had come out with Mary from the house
decisions.reason: They are the visitors of verses 19 and 31, who followed Mary when she went out. They are mourners, not the authorities.

decisions.choice: indignant (L); deeply indignant (B); felt angry (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the note of anger that the verb carries (meaning decision m1), rather than turning it into sorrow. Readable uses the plain word "angry"; Balanced adds "deeply" for the force of the word. A footnote gives "deeply moved".

decisions.choice: the Jews who had come with her
decisions.reason: As in verse 31, Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people in the scene (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Where did you bury him?
alternatives: Where have you laid him? (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Laid" means where the body was put; in plain English the question is where he was buried. The burial was in a cave tomb (verse 38).

decisions.choice: se indignó (L); se indignó profundamente (B); sintió un enojo profundo (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the note of anger the verb carries (meaning decision m1), rather than turning it into sorrow.

decisions.choice: ¿Dónde lo enterraron?
decisions.reason: As in English: says plainly what "where have you laid him" asks. The question is to several people, so it takes the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: s’indigna (L); fut profondément indigné (B); s’est senti en colère (R)
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of anger or sternness wherever else it is used (meaning decision m1). "Frémir", the traditional French rendering, says only that he shuddered, and "ému" turns the anger into sorrow, so every level keeps the note of indignation, as the English does; the footnote on m1 gives "deeply moved". "Esprit" has a small letter because it is Jesus's own inner self (m3); Literal brackets the possessive French needs.

decisions.choice: se troubla {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has "himself" as its object (meaning decision m3). French says "se troubler" with a reflexive "se", which has no setting form; Literal adds the stressed "lui-même", which shows the Greek "himself" and carries the deity_pronoun setting where the English has "Himself". Balanced and Readable say "bouleversé" and "très troublé".

decisions.choice: alighadhibika rohoni (L, B); akasikia hasira ndani kabisa rohoni mwake (R)
decisions.reason: ἐνεβριμήσατο is a strong stirring of anger, as the meaning note says. "Kughadhibika" (to be roused to anger) keeps that, where "kuugua rohoni" (to groan in spirit) or "kuhuzunika" (to grieve) would soften it into sorrow. The same in verse 38.

decisions.choice: "phẫn nộ" (L, B); "giận dữ" (R) for embrimaomai
decisions.reason: The meaning decision finds a strong stirring of anger; "xúc động" (moved) would soften it into grief alone.

decisions.choice: "trong tâm linh" for "in spirit"; "xao động" for "troubled"
decisions.reason: "tâm linh" names the human spirit without suggesting the Holy Spirit; "xao động" is a deep inner shaking, stronger than "bối rối" (confused).

decisions.choice: "분개하시고" (L), "속 깊이 분개하시며" (B), "마음속 깊이 화가 나셨고" (R)
decisions.reason: embrimaomai is a strong stirring of anger (meaning decision); the familiar Korean rendering of grief would remove the anger the decision keeps.

source.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε.

records.literal_gloss: They say to him, "Lord, come and see."

en.L: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, come and see."
en.B: They said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, come and see."

fr.L: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Seigneur, viens et vois. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Seigneur, viens voir. »

vi.L: Họ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Chúa, xin đến mà xem."
vi.B: Họ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Chúa, xin đến xem."
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Thưa Chúa, xin đến mà xem."

decisions.choice: Lord: the address of Mary and those with her who knew him
alternatives: Sir, a polite address from mourners who did not know who Jesus was
decisions.reason: John does not say who answered. Mary had just called him "Lord" (verse 32), and the ones who show him the tomb are those who had come out with her. Some of the speakers may have been visitors from Jerusalem, for whom the word would only be polite ("Sir"), but in this family's company it carries the meaning Mary gave it. A footnote gives "Sir".

decisions.choice: come and see: the words of invitation from the beginning of the Gospel
alternatives: an ordinary phrase with no echo
decisions.reason: Philip said the same words to Nathanael (1:46), and Jesus invited his first followers in very similar words (1:39). There they invite people to come and see Jesus; here they invite Jesus to come and see the place of death. John may intend the echo, but the words are also the natural thing to say.

decisions.choice: They say (Literal); They said (Balanced), They answered (Readable); likewise in verses 38, 39, 40 and 44
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("they say", "he comes") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage (verses 34, 38, 39, 40 and 44).

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: ven y ve (L); ven a ver (B, R)
decisions.reason: The invitation of 1:39 and 1:46, in the same Spanish words as there.

decisions.choice: historic present: "thưa" with no time word (L, here and in 11:38, 11:39, 11:40, 11:44); B and R tell it as past through context
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs do not mark tense; Literal does not add "đã". One decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal ("말한다", "가신다", "말씀하신다"), past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for the historic present (docs/john-terms.md), recorded once for this passage (also 11:38, 11:39, 11:40, 11:44).

decisions.choice: "와서 보십시오" in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: People speaking to Jesus use 합쇼체 (style guide, section 4). The words still echo the invitation "come and see" of chapter 1, though the speech level differs there.

es.R: A Jesús {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} corrían las lágrimas por la cara.

fr.R: Des larmes ont coulé sur le visage de Jésus.

vi.R: Nước mắt Đức Giê-xu tuôn rơi.

decisions.choice: shed tears: a different word from the loud weeping of the mourners
alternatives: wailed, lamented aloud, like the mourners
decisions.reason: The verb means to shed tears and is used only here in the New Testament. Mary and the mourners "weep" with the usual word for crying aloud in grief (verses 31 and 33). John uses another word for Jesus: his grief is real, but it is not the wailing of the mourners.

decisions.choice: wept: a single act told simply; it may mean he began to weep
decisions.reason: The tense tells the event as a whole. It can also mark the start of an action ("began to weep"), but nothing in the context requires that.

decisions.choice: Jesus truly grieves, even though he is about to raise Lazarus
decisions.reason: Jesus knew what he would do (11:11, 23), yet he weeps at his friend's grave. The onlookers read his tears in two ways: as love (verse 36) and as helplessness (verse 37). The Word who "became flesh" (1:14) shares human sorrow.

decisions.choice: shed tears (L); wept (B); Tears ran down Jesus's face (R)
decisions.reason: Literal shows the meaning of the verb and keeps it distinct from the weeping of verses 31 and 33 (meaning decision m1). Balanced keeps the short, familiar sentence. Readable, which says "cry" for the mourners, describes the tears plainly so that the difference stays visible. No level adds anything else to the shortest sentence in the Gospel.

decisions.choice: derramó lágrimas (L); lloró (B); le corrían las lágrimas (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal and Readable keep this verb distinct from the loud weeping of the mourners in verses 31 and 33 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "rơi nước mắt" (L); "khóc" (B); "Nước mắt ... tuôn rơi" (R)
decisions.reason: dakryō is shedding tears, a different word from the loud weeping (klaiō) of Mary and the mourners in 11:33; L and R keep the tears in view.

decisions.choice: "눈물을 흘리셨다" (shed tears), not "우셨다" (wept)
decisions.reason: John uses a different word from the loud weeping of Mary and the mourners ("울다", 11:31-33); Korean keeps the difference with "눈물을 흘리다".

source.text: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἴδε πῶς ἐφίλει αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Were saying therefore the Jews, "See how he was loving him."

en.L: So the Jews were saying, "See how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved him!"
en.B: So the Jews who were there said, "See how much {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved him!"
en.R: The Jews who were watching said, "See how much {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved Lazarus!"

es.L: Decían, pues, los judíos: «¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} cómo lo amaba!».
es.B: Entonces los judíos que estaban allí dijeron: «¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} cuánto lo amaba!».
es.R: Los judíos que estaban mirando dijeron: «¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} cuánto amaba a Lázaro!».

fr.L: Les Juifs disaient donc : « Voyez comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’aimait ! »
fr.B: Les Juifs qui étaient là dirent alors : « Voyez combien {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’aimait ! »
fr.R: Les Juifs qui regardaient ont dit : « Voyez comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aimait Lazare ! »

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi walikuwa wakisema, "Tazama jinsi alivyompenda!"
sw.B: Basi Wayahudi waliokuwa pale wakasema, "Tazama jinsi alivyompenda sana!"
sw.R: Wayahudi waliokuwa wakitazama wakasema, "Tazama jinsi alivyompenda Lazaro sana!"

vi.L: Vậy người Do Thái cứ nói: "Kìa, xem ông ấy yêu anh ấy biết bao!"
vi.B: Vậy những người Do Thái có mặt ở đó nói: "Xem kìa, ông ấy yêu anh ấy biết bao!"
vi.R: Những người Do Thái đứng xem nói: "Xem kìa, ông ấy yêu La-xa-rơ biết bao!"

ko.L: 그래서 유대인들이 말하고 있었다. "보라, 그분이 그를 얼마나 사랑하셨는지!"
ko.B: 그러자 그곳에 있던 유대인들이 말했다. "저분이 그를 얼마나 사랑하셨는지 보아라!"
ko.R: 지켜보던 유대인들이 말했다. "저분이 나사로를 얼마나 사랑하셨는지 좀 봐라!"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the mourners standing by
decisions.reason: They are the same visitors as in verses 31 and 33, who see Jesus's tears. They are mourners, not the authorities.

decisions.choice: loved: warm love for a friend
decisions.reason: This is the verb the sisters used in their message, "the one you love is ill" (11:3). John also uses his other verb for love of Jesus's love for this family (11:5). Both mean love; the onlookers see in his tears how dear Lazarus was to him.

decisions.choice: were saying, loved: several of them said it, and his love was lasting
decisions.reason: The tense of "were saying" suggests the remark passed among them. "Loved" is in a tense that describes an ongoing state: his friendship with Lazarus was long-standing.

decisions.choice: the Jews who were there (B); the Jews who were watching (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 31, Balanced and Readable tie the word John wrote to the people in the scene (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Lazarus
decisions.reason: Readable names Lazarus, since "he" and "him" would refer to two different men in a short sentence.

decisions.choice: los judíos (every level)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners from Jerusalem in this scene (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: aimait (every level)
decisions.reason: This is the verb the sisters used in 11:3; John uses his other verb for love of the same family in 11:5 (meaning decision m2). French uses "aimer" for both, as the shared choices for John set out; a weaker word such as "affection" would make the onlookers say less than they do.

decisions.choice: "ông ấy" for Jesus in the onlookers' words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The mourners are not his disciples; they speak of him with the ordinary respectful "ông ấy", which has no reverent capital form.

decisions.choice: The mourners speak of Jesus with respect ("그분", "저분", "-셨-")
decisions.reason: These are sympathetic mourners speaking of a respected teacher; Korean gives them honorific forms, unlike the critics of 11:37, who say "이 사람".

source.text: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἐδύνατο οὗτος ὁ ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ;

records.literal_gloss: Some but of them said, "Not was able this [one] the [one] having opened the eyes of the blind [man] to make that also this [one] not should die?"

en.L: But some of them said, "Was not this [man], who opened the eyes of the blind [man], able to make it so that this [man] also should not die?"
en.B: But some of them said, "He opened the eyes of the blind man. Was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not able to keep this man from dying as well?"
en.R: But some of them said, "This man gave sight to the man who was born blind. Surely {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could have kept Lazarus from dying too!"

es.L: Pero algunos de ellos dijeron: «¿No podía este, que abrió los ojos del ciego, hacer también que este no muriera?».
es.B: Pero algunos de ellos dijeron: «Él abrió los ojos al ciego. ¿No podía {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hacer que este hombre no muriera?».
es.R: Pero algunos de ellos dijeron: «Este hombre le dio la vista al que nació ciego. ¡Seguro que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} podría haber evitado que Lázaro muriera!».

fr.L: Mais quelques-uns d’entre eux dirent : « Celui-ci, qui a ouvert les yeux de l’aveugle, ne pouvait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas faire en sorte que celui-ci aussi ne meure pas ? »
fr.B: Mais certains d’entre eux dirent : « Il a ouvert les yeux de l’aveugle. Ne pouvait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas empêcher aussi cet homme de mourir ? »
fr.R: Mais certains d’entre eux ont dit : « Cet homme a rendu la vue à celui qui était né aveugle. Il aurait sûrement pu empêcher aussi Lazare de mourir ! »

sw.L: Lakini baadhi yao wakasema, "Je, huyu, aliyefumbua macho ya [yule] kipofu, hakuweza kufanya kwamba huyu naye asife?"
sw.B: Lakini baadhi yao wakasema, "Alifumbua macho ya yule kipofu. Je, hakuweza kumzuia mtu huyu naye asife?"
sw.R: Lakini baadhi yao wakasema, "Mtu huyu alimpa kuona yule aliyezaliwa kipofu. Hakika angeweza kumzuia Lazaro naye asife!"

vi.L: Nhưng có mấy người trong số họ nói: "Người này, là người đã mở mắt người mù, chẳng lẽ lại không thể làm cho người này cũng khỏi chết sao?"
vi.B: Nhưng vài người trong số họ nói: "Ông ấy đã mở mắt người mù. Chẳng lẽ ông ấy lại không thể giữ cho người này khỏi chết sao?"
vi.R: Nhưng một vài người trong số họ nói: "Ông này đã làm cho người mù từ lúc mới sinh được sáng mắt. Chắc chắn ông ấy cũng có thể giữ cho La-xa-rơ khỏi chết chứ!"

ko.L: 그러나 그들 가운데 어떤 사람들은 말했다. "눈먼 사람의 눈을 뜨게 한 이 사람이, 이 사람도 죽지 않게 할 수는 없었단 말이냐?"
ko.B: 그러나 그들 가운데 몇 사람은 말했다. "이 사람은 눈먼 사람의 눈을 뜨게 했다. 그런 그가 이 사람은 죽지 않게 할 수 없었단 말이냐?"
ko.R: 그러나 그들 가운데 몇 사람은 말했다. "이 사람은 날 때부터 눈먼 사람도 보게 해 주었다. 그러니 나사로도 죽지 않게 할 수 있었을 것 아니냐!"

decisions.choice: the blind man: the man born blind whom Jesus healed in Jerusalem (chapter 9)
alternatives: any blind person Jesus had healed
decisions.reason: With the article, "the blind man" points to a case they all knew: the man born blind whose eyes Jesus opened (9:1-7), a sign the people of Jerusalem argued over (9:16; 10:21). These visitors had come from Jerusalem (11:18-19).

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer yes: he could have
alternatives: a real question asking whether he could
decisions.reason: The form of the question assumes that he could have prevented the death. It repeats what Martha and Mary had said (verses 21, 32), but from people standing at a distance.

decisions.choice: a criticism set against the remark before it
alternatives: an expression of regret with no criticism
decisions.reason: John sets these words against "See how he loved him" (verse 36) with "but". The speakers grant his power and question his love or his reasons for staying away. Some hear real puzzlement rather than criticism; the words could carry either.

decisions.choice: Surely he could have
decisions.reason: Readable states the yes that the question expects (meaning decision m2), names Lazarus, and makes clear that "the blind man" is the one of chapter 9 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: He opened the eyes of the blind man. Was he not able ...
alternatives: Could not the one who opened ...
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the healing first as a statement, then the question, which keeps the speakers' point clear without one long question.

decisions.choice: ¡Seguro que él podría ...!
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable states the yes the question expects (meaning decision m2). "Él" at the start of the B sentence is written plain.

decisions.choice: "이 사람" for Jesus, without honorifics; "-단 말이냐" (L, B), "-것 아니냐" (R)
decisions.reason: The speakers are critical (meaning decision), so Korean does not give them the respect of 11:36; the endings carry a question that expects the answer yes.

source.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν πάλιν ἐμβριμώμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔρχεται εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· ἦν δὲ σπήλαιον, καὶ λίθος ἐπέκειτο ἐπ’ αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Jesus therefore again being indignant in himself comes to the tomb; it was now a cave, and a stone was lying upon it.

en.L: So Jesus, again indignant within {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, comes to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
en.B: Jesus, once more deeply indignant within {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay over the entrance.
en.R: Jesus was angry again deep inside as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone covering the opening.

es.L: Jesús, pues, indignado de nuevo dentro de {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}, llega al sepulcro. Era una cueva, y una piedra estaba puesta encima de ella.
es.B: Jesús, profundamente indignado otra vez dentro de {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}, llegó al sepulcro. Era una cueva, y una piedra tapaba la entrada.
es.R: Jesús volvió a sentir un enojo profundo mientras llegaba a la tumba. Era una cueva con una piedra que tapaba la abertura.

fr.L: Jésus donc, de nouveau indigné en {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, vient au tombeau. Or c’était une grotte, et une pierre reposait contre elle.
fr.B: Jésus, de nouveau profondément indigné en {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, arriva au tombeau. C’était une grotte, et une pierre en fermait l’entrée.
fr.R: Jésus était encore en colère au plus profond de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est arrivé à la tombe. C’était une grotte, avec une pierre qui en bouchait l’ouverture.

sw.L: Basi Yesu, akighadhibika tena ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, anakuja kaburini. Basi lilikuwa pango, na jiwe lilikuwa limewekwa juu yake.
sw.B: Yesu, akighadhibika sana tena ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, alifika kaburini. Lilikuwa pango, na jiwe lilikuwa limewekwa mlangoni pake.
sw.R: Yesu alisikia hasira tena ndani kabisa alipofika kaburini. Lilikuwa pango lenye jiwe lililofunika mlango wake.

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu, lại phẫn nộ trong mình, đi đến mộ. Bấy giờ đó là một cái hang, và có một tảng đá chặn trên đó.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu, một lần nữa vô cùng phẫn nộ trong lòng, đi đến mộ. Đó là một cái hang, có một tảng đá chặn ngay cửa.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lại thấy giận dữ sâu trong lòng khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi đến mộ. Mộ là một cái hang, có tảng đá lấp lối vào.

ko.L: 그래서 예수께서 다시 속으로 분개하시며 무덤으로 가신다. 그것은 굴이었는데, 돌 하나가 그 위에 놓여 있었다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 다시 속 깊이 분개하시며 무덤으로 가셨다. 무덤은 굴이었고, 입구는 돌로 막혀 있었다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 다시 마음속 깊이 화가 나신 채 무덤으로 가셨다. 무덤은 굴이었는데, 돌 하나가 입구를 막고 있었다.

decisions.choice: again indignant within himself: the same anger as in verse 33, still stirring as he comes
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 33 (see the note there), here in a form that shows the feeling going on as he walks to the tomb. "Within himself" matches "in spirit" (verse 33): this is inward, not an outburst at those around him. It comes straight after the criticism of verse 37.

decisions.choice: a cave tomb: a burial chamber in the rock, closed with a stone
alternatives: a grave dug in the ground
decisions.reason: Families around Jerusalem buried their dead in chambers cut into the rock or in natural caves, and the opening was closed with a heavy stone against animals and the smell. Jesus's own tomb had a stone as well (20:1). Moving such a stone needed several people (verse 41).

decisions.choice: a stone lay against it: the stone closed the opening
alternatives: a stone lay on top of it, over an opening in the ground
decisions.reason: The words fit either a stone set against a doorway in a hillside or a stone over an opening cut down into the rock. John does not say which; the point is that the tomb was shut.

decisions.choice: indignant (L, B); angry (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as in verse 33, so that readers see that the same feeling returns.

decisions.choice: over the entrance (B); covering the opening (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the stone covered, without deciding the shape of the tomb (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: indignado (L, B); enojo (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as in verse 33, so the same feeling is seen to return (meaning decision m1).

source.text: λέγει ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρατε τὸν λίθον.

records.literal_gloss: Says the Jesus, "Take away the stone."

fr.R: Jésus a dit : « Déplacez la pierre. »

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Hãy cất tảng đá đi."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo: "Hãy dời tảng đá đi."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Hãy đẩy tảng đá sang một bên."

decisions.choice: take away: a command to the people standing there
alternatives: a command to his disciples only
decisions.reason: The command is plural. Jesus has the bystanders do what people can do; only the raising itself is his. He does the same at the end (verse 44).

decisions.choice: opening a tomb after burial: a shocking request
decisions.reason: Once a body was laid in a tomb and the stone was in place, the tomb was not opened again except for a new burial. Contact with a grave made a person unclean (Numbers 19:16), and the body would already be decaying, as Martha says next.

decisions.choice: Move the stone away
decisions.reason: "Move" is plain and does not assume that the stone could be rolled (see verse 38).

decisions.choice: plural command
decisions.reason: The command is plural, to the bystanders (meaning decision m1), so it takes the ustedes / vosotros setting.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τοῦ τετελευτηκότος Μάρθα· Κύριε, ἤδη ὄζει, τεταρταῖος γάρ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the sister of the [one] having died, Martha, "Lord, already he stinks, a fourth-day [one] for he is."

en.L: The sister of the dead [man], Martha, says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, already he stinks, for he is four days [dead]."
en.B: Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, he already stinks; this is the fourth day."
en.R: Martha, the dead man's sister, said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "But Lord, he already stinks! He has been dead for four days."

es.L: Le dice Marta, la hermana del muerto: «Señor, ya hiede, porque es [el] cuarto día».
es.B: Marta, la hermana del muerto, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Señor, ya apesta; es el cuarto día».
es.R: Marta, la hermana del muerto, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Pero, Señor, ¡ya apesta! Lleva cuatro días muerto».

fr.L: La sœur du mort, Marthe, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Seigneur, il sent déjà mauvais, car c’est son quatrième jour. »
fr.B: Marthe, la sœur du mort, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Seigneur, il sent déjà mauvais : c’est le quatrième jour. »
fr.R: Marthe, la sœur du mort, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Mais Seigneur, il sent déjà mauvais ! Il est mort depuis quatre jours. »

sw.L: Dada wa yule aliyekufa, Martha, anamwambia, "Bwana, tayari ananuka, kwa maana ni siku nne [tangu afe]."
sw.B: Martha, dada wa yule aliyekufa, akamwambia, "Bwana, tayari ananuka; hii ni siku ya nne."
sw.R: Martha, dada wa yule aliyekufa, akamwambia, "Lakini Bwana, tayari ananuka! Amekuwa amekufa kwa siku nne."

vi.L: Em gái của người chết là Ma-thê thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Chúa, anh ấy đã bốc mùi rồi, vì đã [chết] bốn ngày."
vi.B: Ma-thê, em gái của người chết, thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Chúa, anh con đã bốc mùi rồi, vì đây là ngày thứ tư."
vi.R: Ma-thê, em gái người chết, thưa: "Nhưng thưa Chúa, anh con đã bốc mùi rồi! Anh ấy chết đã bốn ngày rồi."

ko.L: 죽은 사람의 자매 마르다가 그분께 말한다. "주님, 벌써 그에게서 냄새가 납니다. 나흘째이기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 죽은 사람의 자매 마르다가 그분께 말했다. "주님, 벌써 냄새가 납니다. 나흘이나 되었습니다."
ko.R: 죽은 나사로의 자매 마르다가 말했다. "하지만 주님, 벌써 썩는 냄새가 납니다. 죽은 지 나흘이나 되었습니다."

decisions.choice: already he stinks: a blunt statement of what she is sure of
alternatives: there will be a smell (a softer expression)
decisions.reason: The verb is the plain word for giving off a bad smell. The tomb is still shut, so Martha says what she knows must be true: after four days the body is decaying. Her words are blunt, and the story keeps them so.

decisions.choice: the fourth day: decay had begun and all hope was gone
decisions.reason: Burial took place on the day of death, and Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days (11:17). In a hot climate decay was well under way by then. A belief recorded in later Jewish writings held that the soul stayed near the body for three days; whether or not Martha thought of it, by the fourth day no one could doubt that he was dead.

decisions.choice: the sister of the dead man: John names her by her loss at this moment
decisions.reason: Martha is well known to the reader by now (11:1, 5, 20-27). Calling her "the sister of the dead man" here stresses that the one in the tomb is truly dead, and shows why she objects.

decisions.choice: stinks
decisions.reason: Every level keeps Martha's plain word (meaning decision m1); a polite word would soften what she says.

decisions.choice: But Lord
decisions.reason: Readable shows that she is objecting to the command just given.

decisions.choice: hiede (L); apesta (B, R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps Martha's blunt word (meaning decision m1); "huele mal" would soften it.

decisions.choice: il sent déjà mauvais (every level)
decisions.reason: Martha's word is the plain verb for a bad smell, and the story keeps it blunt (meaning decision m1). "Il sent déjà" with no adjective is the polite turn that would soften her words; "il pue" is as blunt as the Greek but sounds coarse when read aloud in French. "Il sent mauvais" says plainly what she means; a native reviewer may prefer "il pue".

decisions.choice: "bốc mùi" for "stinks"
decisions.reason: Martha speaks bluntly; "bốc mùi" is plain without being coarse.

decisions.choice: "em gái" for Martha as Lazarus's sister
decisions.reason: Follows the choice of Lazarus as the elder brother (11:2), which the Greek does not settle.

decisions.choice: "냄새가 납니다" (L, B); "썩는 냄새가 납니다" (R), in polite 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Martha's statement is blunt but addressed to her Lord; Korean keeps the bluntness in the content and the respect in the ending. Readable says plainly what the smell is.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: Says to her the Jesus, "Not said I to you that if you should believe you will see the glory of the God?"

en.L: Jesus says to her, "Did I not say to you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"
en.B: Jesus said to her, "Did I not tell you that you would see the glory of God if you believed?"
en.R: Jesus said to her, "Did I not tell you? If you believe, you will see the glory of God."

es.L: Le dice Jesús: «¿No te dije que, si crees, verás la gloria de Dios?».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «¿No te dije que verías la gloria de Dios si creías?».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «¿No te lo dije? Si crees, verás la gloria de Dios».

fr.L: Jésus lui dit : « Ne t’ai-je pas dit que, si tu crois, tu verras la gloire de Dieu ? »
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Ne t’ai-je pas dit que tu verrais la gloire de Dieu si tu croyais ? »
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Est-ce que je ne te l’ai pas dit ? Si tu crois, tu verras la gloire de Dieu. »

sw.L: Yesu anamwambia, "Je, mimi sikukuambia kwamba ikiwa utaamini, utautazama utukufu wa Mungu?"
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Je, sikukuambia kwamba ungeuona utukufu wa Mungu ikiwa ungeamini?"
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Je, sikukuambia? Ukiamini, utaona utukufu wa Mungu."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với cô: "Chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với con rằng nếu con tin, con sẽ thấy vinh quang của Đức Chúa Trời sao?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo cô: "Chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã bảo con rằng con sẽ thấy vinh quang của Đức Chúa Trời nếu con tin sao?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với cô: "Ta đã chẳng nói với con rồi sao? Nếu con tin, con sẽ thấy vinh quang của Đức Chúa Trời."

decisions.choice: Did I not tell you: pointing back to his words about God's glory and about believing
alternatives: a saying to Martha not recorded
decisions.reason: John has not given these exact words to Martha. Jesus said that the illness was "for the glory of God" (11:4), and he told Martha that whoever believes in him will live (11:25-26). He now joins the two.

decisions.choice: the glory of God: God's power and presence made visible in what Jesus does
decisions.reason: In John the glory of God is seen in Jesus (1:14) and shown in his signs (2:11). The raising of Lazarus will show it, and it will also lead to the cross, where Jesus is glorified (11:4; 12:23).

decisions.choice: if you believe, you will see: trust now, and sight follows
alternatives: seeing as a reward that depends on how strong her faith is
decisions.reason: The condition looks to what she will do now: trust him enough to let the stone be moved. Believing comes first, and then she will see.

decisions.choice: that you would see the glory of God if you believed
alternatives: that if you believe, you will see (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the promise first and the condition after it, a natural order in this language that keeps the same meaning.

decisions.choice: "con" for Martha, as in 11:23-26
decisions.reason: Jesus keeps the form he used with Martha earlier in the chapter.

fr.B: Alors Jésus leva les yeux et dit : « Père, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rends grâce parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as exaucé. \v 42 Moi, je savais bien que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}exauces toujours. Mais j’ai parlé à cause de la foule qui se tient autour de nous, pour qu’ils croient que c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé. »

Mais j’ai dit cela à voix haute pour les gens qui sont ici. Je veux qu’ils croient que c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé. »

vi.B: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu ngước mắt lên và nói: "Thưa Cha, Con tạ ơn Cha vì Cha đã nghe Con. \v 42 Chính Con biết Cha luôn luôn nghe Con. Nhưng Con nói vậy là vì đám đông đang đứng quanh đây, để họ tin rằng chính Cha đã sai Con."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu ngước mắt nhìn lên trời và nói: "Thưa Cha, cảm ơn Cha đã nghe Con. \v 42 Con biết Cha luôn nghe Con. Nhưng Con nói lớn tiếng như vậy là vì những người đang đứng đây. Con muốn họ tin rằng Cha đã sai Con."

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 눈을 위로 들고 말씀하셨다. "아버지, 제 말을 들으신 것을 감사드립니다. \v 42 아버지께서 언제나 제 말을 들으신다는 것을 저는 알고 있었습니다. 그러나 둘러서 있는 무리 때문에 [이렇게] 말씀드렸습니다. 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것을 그들이 믿게 하려는 것입니다."
ko.B: 예수께서 눈을 들어 위를 바라보시며 말씀하셨다. "아버지, 제 말을 들어 주셔서 감사합니다. \v 42 아버지께서 언제나 제 말을 들어 주신다는 것을 저는 알고 있었습니다. 그러나 제가 이렇게 말씀드리는 것은 여기 둘러서 있는 무리를 위해서입니다. 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것을 그들이 믿게 하려는 것입니다."

decisions.choice: lifted his eyes upward: a posture of prayer toward heaven
decisions.reason: People often prayed looking up to heaven (Psalm 123:1). Jesus does the same when he gives thanks for the loaves (Mark 6:41) and when he prays before his death (17:1).

decisions.choice: you heard me: thanks for a prayer already answered, before Lazarus comes out
alternatives: thanks for a prayer spoken aloud just before
decisions.reason: John has not recorded the prayer that the Father heard; Jesus may have prayed earlier, as Martha expected (11:22). He gives thanks as for something already done. The raising is the Father's answer, and Jesus is sure of it before anyone sees it.

decisions.choice: I knew that you always hear me: Jesus did not need to say it for his own sake
decisions.reason: The "I" is emphatic and "always" sets this prayer within a constant relationship (compare 8:29). He did not give thanks aloud because he had doubted; the next words say why he spoke.

decisions.choice: for the sake of the crowd, so that they may believe that you sent me
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks aloud so that the people will understand that what follows comes from the Father in answer to the Son, not from any power of his own apart from God (5:19, 30). The aim is that they believe he was sent by the Father, a constant theme of the Gospel (5:36-38; 17:21). The "you" is emphatic: it was the Father who sent him.

decisions.choice: you, me (in Jesus's prayer)
decisions.reason: The "you" that Jesus addresses to the Father and the "me" with which he speaks of himself use the deity_pronoun setting, like every other pronoun for God or Christ.

decisions.choice: I myself; it was you who (B); toward heaven, out loud (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the emphatic "I" and "you" (meaning decisions m3 and m4). Readable says where he looked (meaning decision m1) and makes plain that the thanks was said aloud so the crowd could hear.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}
decisions.reason: The stressed "tú" for the Father takes the setting, and so do "te" for the Father and "me" for Jesus, by the book-wide rule for Spanish (see 8:12); Readable's "escucharme" is joined to the verb and stays plain.

decisions.choice: Yo ya sabía; fuiste tú quien
decisions.reason: As in English: shows the emphatic "I" and "you" (meaning decisions m3, m4).

decisions.choice: tu m’as entendu (L); tu m’as exaucé (B); merci de m’avoir écouté (R)
decisions.reason: Of prayer, the Greek verb means that God heard and granted it (meaning decision m2). French has a verb for exactly that, "exaucer", which Balanced uses; Literal keeps the plain "entendre", and Readable says "écouter", the everyday word. Jesus says "tu" to the Father, as everyone in French says "tu" to God; every pronoun in the prayer takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "Cha" for "you" and "Con" for "I/me" in Jesus's prayer, with no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Style guide sections 6-7: Jesus speaks to the Father as "Cha" and of himself as "Con"; these are nouns, always capitalised, so the English pronoun spans have no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "ngước mắt" with no possessive
decisions.reason: Vietnamese does not need "his" with a body part here, so the English bracketed "[his]" has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: Jesus prays to the Father in 합쇼체, with the humble "저", "제" and "말씀드리다"; "아버지께서" stands for "you"
decisions.reason: The style guide sets 합쇼체 for Jesus speaking to the Father. Korean does not address a father with a pronoun, so "아버지" is repeated.

decisions.choice: "[이렇게] 말씀드렸습니다"
decisions.reason: Korean needs to say what was said; the Greek leaves the object implied.

ko.L: 그리고 이 말씀을 하시고 큰 소리로 외치셨다. "나사로야, 이리 나오너라!"

decisions.choice: the voice that calls the dead out: the fulfilment in small of 5:25-29
decisions.reason: Jesus had said that the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God and live, and that all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out (5:25, 28-29). Here one man in a tomb hears his voice and comes out. The shepherd also calls his own by name (10:3).

decisions.choice: cried out: a loud shout
alternatives: a spoken command in an ordinary voice
decisions.reason: The verb means to shout. John uses it of the crowds at Jesus's entry into Jerusalem (12:13) and at his trial (18:40; 19:6, 15). With "a loud voice" it shows that everyone could hear the command; it was not a whispered formula.

decisions.choice: here, out: come out
decisions.reason: The Greek is two short words, "here" (used as a command, "come") and "out". Together they are a sharp call: "Come out!"

decisions.choice: After these words
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the shout closely to the prayer just spoken, which is the point of the Greek phrase.

decisions.choice: ¡sal fuera!
decisions.reason: Two short Greek words, "here" and "out", make a command (meaning decision m3); "sal fuera" says it as briefly.

decisions.choice: "이리 나오너라" (L); "나오너라" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is two adverbs, "here, out"; Literal keeps "이리" (here) and Balanced and Readable say it as the plain command.

ko.B: 그러자 죽었던 사람이 나왔다. 손발은 천으로 감겨 있었고, 얼굴은 수건으로 싸여 있었다.

decisions.choice: the one who had died: the dead man himself came out
decisions.reason: John calls him by what he had been: the man who had died. His coming out answers the command "come out" (verse 43) and echoes 5:29. John tells it in the plainest words.

decisions.choice: strips of cloth and a face cloth: the wrappings of burial
decisions.reason: The body was wrapped for burial, with strips of cloth binding the feet and hands and a smaller cloth around the face. The word for the face cloth is used again of the cloth that had been on Jesus's head, which lay folded in its own place in the empty tomb (20:7). Lazarus comes out still bound and will one day die again; Jesus leaves his wrappings behind.

decisions.choice: bound feet and hands: still in the wrappings as he came out
alternatives: he came out free of them
decisions.reason: John does not explain how a man bound in this way could come out. The point of the detail is that he was a man prepared for the grave, and that others still had to set him free (the next sentence).

decisions.choice: Out came the man who had been dead
alternatives: The man who had died came out
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the verb first, as the Greek does, for the force of the moment.

decisions.choice: still
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the wrappings were still on him as he came out (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Y salió el que ...

decisions.choice: to them: to the bystanders
decisions.reason: The commands are plural and are given to those standing near, as the command about the stone was (verse 39). Jesus raises the dead man; others free him from the wrappings.

decisions.choice: let him go: allow him to go away freely
decisions.reason: The verb means to let or allow, and "go" is the ordinary word for going away. Once unbound, Lazarus is free to go home with his sisters (see 12:1-2).

decisions.choice: Untie him (B); Take the cloths off him (R)
decisions.reason: "Loose" is old-fashioned in this sense. Readable says plainly what was to be untied.

decisions.choice: Quítenle las vendas
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what was to be untied. The commands are plural (meaning decision m1).
